coverage: Airliners: 62% of flights have both airports matched and 38% are partly observed (all US aircraft incl. general aviation: 43% and 51%).
20% of partly observed flights are simply split at midnight UTC; the rest lost coverage mid-flight (median silence 89 min).
Leg continuity is 100% over 68 consecutive airliner legs: each landing airport matched the next takeoff airport.
Published route tables agree with our departure airport 68% and arrival 72% of the time; our airports appear somewhere in the published itinerary 75%+ of the time.
fleet: The oldest common US airliner type is the Boeing 757-200 (median 32 years); the youngest is the Boeing 737 MAX 8 (3).
21% of US airliners are registered to a bank, trust or lessor rather than the airline that flies them.
Hardest-working fleet in the sample: Southwest Airlines, 8.4 airborne hours per aircraft per flying day.
Business jets opt out of public tracking (FAA LADD/PIA) at the highest rate: 27% of those seen flying, vs 7% of piston aircraft.
